observation: Actual full-resolution durable original PNG opened separately once before drawing; no old figure or answer evidence used.
inventory: One p-V family with origin 0, upward pressure arrow and rightward volume arrow; no numeric ticks or units.
Five solid isotherms are visible, labelled T, T1, T2, critical Tk and T3. T, T1 and T2 have three progressively higher and shorter horizontal coexistence plateaus.
The critical curve is bold and has a locally horizontal tangent at labelled K; the upper T3 curve has no finite horizontal coexistence plateau.
One dashed two-sided coexistence envelope passes through all six subcritical plateau endpoints and K, ending at the volume axis on both sides.
A solid horizontal critical-pressure guide runs from the pressure axis to K. Solid volume guides descend to the volume axis from the low-temperature endpoints, middle-temperature endpoints and K.
The original bottom labels from left to right are V2, V2-prime, critical Vk, V1-prime, V1. These source families reverse the convention already established in fig54 and n38.
The two higher-temperature T2 plateau endpoints are visible on the dashed envelope but have no additional printed bottom volume labels or extra vertical guides.
All source curve endpoints are finite and retained; no extrapolated high-pressure branch, new temperature value or added cycle is warranted.
additions: Registered modern endpoint notation: source left V2/V2-prime display V1/V1-prime; source right V1-prime/V1 display V2-prime/V2. This is an explicitly declared correction, not claimed source lettering.
English c denotes critical in p_c, V_c and T_c; source point K stays K. Source temperature indices T1, T2 and T3 remain indices, not numeric temperature readings.

Axis-wise affine drawing scaling and tiered bottom labels retain source volume order without assigning calibrated physical coordinates. The full current n38 and n39 title/prose/captions and n39 shared attachment are bound.
uncertainties: The hand-drawn curves are qualitative and uncalibrated. Internal drawing coordinates and slopes are not supplied thermodynamic data.
